# NOTES ON THE FIVE BOOKS (compact reference)

## BOOK 1 — *A Monk of Cruta* (E. Phillips Oppenheim, 1894 Gutenberg #31535)

**Preface/frame:** Title page, Contents (36 chapters; "Adrea's Diary" interludes at ch. IV, XI, XXI, XXVIII–XXXI).

**Setting/people:** Island monastery of Cruta (Mediterranean/Greek-style island). Father Adrian (tall, gaunt priest, Jesuit-like; later revealed as Adrea's/Irene's son and Count of Cruta's grandson). Martin de Vaux (dying, owner of Vaux Abbey, Northumbrian; shot Victor/Victor Ferdinand Hirsfeld? — he shoots Victor, the Count Hirsfeld). Gomez (servant). Victor Ferdinand Hirsfeld (Count; Martin's enemy, killed by Martin's pistol shot at Cruta). Paul de Vaux (son, heir, ~30s, Mrs. Mother = Mrs./Lady de Vaux; Arthur de Vaux (younger brother, Aldershot officer, infatuated with dancer). Adrea Kiros (dancer; "little brown girl"; orphan; daughter of Count Hirsfeld's associate murdered by Martin; Adrea's diary). Lady May Westover (fair, grey-eyed, Paul's intended; brother Captain Westover). Captain Leslie Horton; Dick Carruthers; Lord Westover. Madame de Merteuill (= Irene, Count of Cruta's daughter; Adrian's mother; Martin's wife). Count of Cruta (Irene's father; grandfather of Adrian; "Lord of Cruta"; threatens; burns castle; dies). Count Hirsfeld / "Count Victor Ferdinand Hirsfeld" (friend of Irene). Sister Elise (convent). Father Andrew (monk). Guiseppe (fisherman, rescuer). Lord of Cruta's servants; Marie (maid, personated Irene at wedding).

**Plot in order:**
1. Storm; dying Martin de Vaux at Cruta monastery with priest Father Adrian and servant Gomez; yacht arrives (Paul steering). Visitor Victor (Count Hirsfeld) and Paul enter. Martin shoots Victor, dies; Martin dies; Adrea (child) present.
2. Paul at Lady Swindon's afternoon; dancer Adrea Kiros performs; Paul and Adrea share a cab; Paul's brother Arthur sees.
3. Paul at Vaux Abbey; Mrs. de Vaux; priest seen at Abbey; Reynolds the servant.
4. Lady May & Paul ride; Arthur infatuated; priest Adrian in avenue.
5. Paul with Adrea in London; Arthur borrows/has acceptance; Adrea's flat at 18 Grey Street; letter pleading.
6. Adrea's diary: Grey Street, Father Adrian's visits; Adrea wears no name; "Spanish"/monastery of St. Bernard.
7. Father Adrian confronts Paul in ruins; threatens; "a week."
8. Adrea gets Paul/Adrian quarrel; Adrian threatens Adrea; Gomez involved; Adrea kills Adrian with dagger in Ch. XXX–XXXI; Gomez hides; Adrea's rendezvous; Father Adrian stabbed by Adrea in the monastery of St. Bernard chair; body taken to wood.
9. Chs. XXXII–XXXV: Count of Cruta (old, gaunt, "Lord of Cruta"); Guiseppe's fishermen; Paul goes to Cruta on yacht; dying Madame de Merteuill (Irene) reveals story; Count of Cruta reveals plot; castle burns; Guiseppe rescues Paul.
10. Ch. XXXVI: Adrea's final diary; Florence; Gomez warns; Paul leaves; Adrea takes poison; Paul returns too late. "THE END."
Ad: advertisements for *The Mystery of the Ravenspurs* (Fred M. White) and *The Peer and the Woman*.

---

## BOOK 2 — *The Yellow House; Master of Men* (E. Phillips Oppenheim, Gutenberg #41402)

**People:** Rev. Horace Ffolliot (curate-in-charge, Northshire; alias Philip Maltabar; Canon Ffolliot); Kate Ffolliot (narrator, elder daughter; black-haired, pale, ~20); Alice Ffolliot (younger, literal, pious). Lady Naselton (Amy; matchmaker; godmother to Bruce). Bruce Deville (of Deville Court; untidy, beagler, brusque; dog "Lawless"; mare "Diana"). Adelaide Fortress/Mrs. Fortress (Yellow House; Socialist; real mother of Kate; ex-lover of Horace; "Marcia"). Olive Berdenstein (sister of Stephen Berdenstein; plain, rich, prominent teeth, diamonds; pursues Bruce). Stephen Berdenstein (South American, Rio; victim, murdered, Martin/Horace). Berdenstein's cabinet photograph. Mr. Berdenstein-Blackmailer; Mr. Charlsworth; Bishop of Exchester; Mr. Hewitt; Naselton Hall; Mr. Harris (Greek manuscript); Gabriel... ; Judas accusations.

**Plot:** Vicar arrives; Lady Naselton gossips about Yellow House and Bruce; Bruce's dog bandaged by Kate; Ffolliot & Bruce quarrel; Adelaide's tea; Kate learns mother = Adelaide, father Horace's secret; Stephen Berdenstein visits; murdered in plantation; Horace's revolver; Berdenstein's sister Olive comes; photo "Philip Maltabar" found; Horace leaves for London; Mrs. Fortress's secret ("I was that woman"); Olive proposes; Bruce proposes; Olive's compact; Kate & Bruce engaged; Horace confesses; Horace dies in Whitechapel "Colville Hall" (East End mission); "This is happiness."

Transcriber corrections listed at end.

## BOOK 3 — *American Boys Afloat; or, Cruising in the Orient* (Oliver Optic, Gutenberg #75149, 1893)

**Dedication:** to Dr. William P. Leavitt. Preface by William T. Adams.

**Characters:** Louis Belgrave (17, millionaire, steam-yacht Guardian-Mother); Felix McGavonty (Irish, "Felix", brogue; captain's clerk); Morris Woolridge (14; son of Lowell Woolridge; Blanche's brother); Scott Fencelowe (George Scott; reformed; ex-Seahound, "middy"); Captain Royal Ringgold (commander); Uncle Moses Scarburn (trustee, lawyer, 226 lb); Dr. Philip Hawkes; Prof. Pierre Giroud; Mrs. Belgrave; Mrs. Blossom; Blanche Woolridge (16); Felipe Garcias (Spanish engineer); Giles Chickworth (owner of Salihé); Gray (Scotch smuggler); Diego Velazquez (captain of Golondrina); Judge Salazar; Ali-Noury Pacha (Fatimé, Mogadore); John Donald (oiler); Pitts (cook); Don (second engineer); Mr. Boulong (first officer).

**Sequence:** Salihé alongside; Chickworth's excursion; smugglers (Gray, Velazquez) take Salihé at Palmones River; big four lasso Gray; prisoners; Salihé recaptured; Algeciras court (Judge Salazar; Louis testifies "My mother is with me"); Gibraltar tour; Salihé bought, renamed **Maud**; Tangier excursion; Pacha's Fatimé chases Maud; Scott's navigation; Maud escapes; Donald picked up; Maud sets out alone (to Malta); water casks leaking; Alboran felucca; gale; foresail reefed; meeting with Guardian-Mother; Algiers lecture by Giroud; Constantinople; dancing dervishes; Pacha's second attempt; Fatimé in Golden Horn.

## BOOK 4 — *The Great White Army* (Max Pemberton, 1916, Gutenberg #35540)

**Frame:** Narrator Surgeon-Major Janil de Constant (Vélites of Guard; taught French, Leipzig; former professor Paris). Nephew Captain Léon de Courcelles (Vélites, handsome, flirtatious). Valerie St. Antoine (dancer-like beautiful Frenchwoman, Prince Nicholas Boris's ward; father Colonel St. Antoine; brother René). Prince Nicholas (Russian assassin, loses arm at guillotine). Prince Boris (house). Heriot (dandy servant). Sergeant Bourgogne; Sergeant Bardot ("antelope"); Gascogne (Léon's servant); Joan d'Izambert (14, rescued); Gabriel d'Izambert (pontonnier); General d'Izambert; Madame Zchekofsky & daughter Kyra (prophetess, at Liadoui); Zayde (girl with treasure, Prince Karasin's jewels); Petrovka (Druobona girl, false peasant, saved from hanging); Payard (captain of dragoons, cormorant; killed by Tcharnhoff); Madame Pauline (Frenchwoman, Russian mistress; kills Tcharnhoff); Ferdinand Tcharnhoff (colonel); Major Duhesne; Count Rafalovitch; Isidore (Jew guide); Ali... ; Gros-Jean.

**Plot:** Entry to Moscow Sept 14, 1812; Heriot lures Constant; dead youth (artist from Fréjus); lackey François kills him; Valerie found in chapel; roof escape; fire; Russians; Léon's rescue; Moscow pillage; Léon's love for Valerie; Ivan's Tower guillotine by Nicholas; Bardot shoots bell; treasure with Zayde; monastery; monks' ruse; wolves; Krasnoë; Liadoui (Emperor visits Mme Zchekofsky; Constant plays drunk, saves Emperor); snow march, Slawkowo church, Valerie's father dies, Valerie vanishes with Emperor; Payard & Pauline dinner; wolves; Bérézina (Gabriel; ford; Valerie & Joan swim); Kovno; Cossack farmhouse; Elbing prison, Prefect Immo von Gustorf; marshal's review ends. "Last review."

## BOOK 5 — *Emmanuel Appadocca; or, Blighted Life* (Maxwell Philip, 1854, 2 vols; Gutenberg #75313, 75314)

**Dedication:** to Harry Daniels. Preface: Trinidad setting, slavery.

**Characters:** Emmanuel Appadocca (pirate captain; quadroon; mother's son; father = James Willmington, Trinidad planter/merchant who abandoned him; mother was a wronged girl). James Willmington. Charles Hamilton (friend, son of Commander, midshipman/officer on British ship). Commander (Mr. Hamilton senior). Lorenzo (Appadocca's chief officer; loves Agnes). Agnes (priest's ward; daughter of Trinidad planter; father is her guardian's friend). Father (priest; Agnes's guardian). Jack Jimmy (Appadocca's negro servant, comic dialect). Jim Splice (English sailor). Feliciana (Venezuelan Ranchero's daughter, in love with Appadocca; later mad). Sebastian (watch officer); Gregoire; Baptiste; Gustave; Domingo; José; Jose; Pedro; Juancito (Llaneros); Llononois (buccaneer in anecdotes); Mrs. Willmington; Bekky (servant).

**Plot:** Vol I: Jack Jimmy & master captured in fishing boat; Black Schooner (death's head); Lorenzo's reconnaissance; capture of "Letitia" ship; sale of prisoners; Willmington tied to cask and cast adrift; Appadocca's cynicism; Hamilton's visits; Appadocca's life history (mother's death, father, pseudo-philosophy); Lorenzo's letter to Agnes; Hamilton offers escape; man-of-war attacks cabin; shark ruins rescue. Vol II: Agnes returned; Willmington arrested on Trinidad; Appadocca captured at St Thomas; hurricane in Dragon's Mouth; Appadocca jumps overboard; rescued by Llaneros; Feliciana; Appadocca escapes; Lorenzo's rescue; Appadocca's villa challenge to Charles; Willmington dragged off; schooner wrecked; Willmington dies in torture-room; Appadocca jumps into sea; Jack Jimmy buries him; Feliciana mad over grave.
